shots.intent: Open with a sharp contrast between institutional IP and a customer-ready object.
label_requirements: Use a split-screen typographic contrast.
Left: patent-document silhouette labeled as an abstract permission slip.
Right: finished orthotic silhouette labeled as a tangible product.
Do not imply any specific patent, product, or clinical claim.

shots.intent: Make the InLoop example physically legible while preserving its claimed, development-stage framing.
label_requirements: Illustrate a generic podiatry-office workflow: foot scan, 3D printer, metal-foam orthotic, next-day handoff.
Use clearly conceptual/non-photoreal visual treatment; no fabricated product photography.
Prominently qualify the timing as a claim: Claimed: 24-hour turnaround.
Include attribution for the workflow and turnaround claim.
shots.source_label: Northeastern University Center for Research Innovation, 2026

shots.intent: Draw a hard boundary between reported development activity and market or clinical proof.
label_requirements: Present three crossed-out proof standards: clinical validation, broad availability, durable demand.
Keep the visual declarative rather than disclaimer-heavy.
Frame the preceding InLoop details as CRI-reported milestones.
Include source attribution.
shots.source_label: Northeastern University Center for Research Innovation, 2026

shots.intent: Show that a high-volume commercialization scoreboard can look impressive without answering the survival question.
label_requirements: Use a labeled horizontal bar chart titled CRI-reported FY2026 activity.
Plot the five count metrics. Treat $25.7M additional spinout fundraising as a separate typography callout, not a bar on the count axis.
Include source attribution.
shots.source_label: Northeastern University Center for Research Innovation, 2026

shots.intent: Reframe commercialization around the narrower survival measure: active companies versus companies ever built.
label_requirements: Use a simple cohort chart, not a survival-rate claim.
Label the 61 figure as CRI listed active, not surviving, successful, or operating.
Include source attribution.
shots.screen_text: Starting is an event. Surviving is the test.
shots.source_label: Northeastern University Center for Research Innovation, 2026

shots.intent: Close on the thesis: university commercialization matters only when research becomes durable customer-facing companies.
label_requirements: Create an illustrated pipeline from lab bench to a sequence of generic sectors: orthotics, microbes, edge AI, network automation, thermal management.
End at a storefront, clinic, factory floor, or customer handoff—not a patent office.
Avoid depicting named companies as proven products or commercially deployed systems.
Use the visual transition from campus/lab to customer setting as the central metaphor.
Include attribution for the development-stage technology examples.
shots.screen_text: The patent is not the product
shots.source_label: Northeastern University Center for Research Innovation, 2026; Cynthia McCormick Hibbert, 2022
